Bit Dark: Hi everyone! Wanted to introduce myself. I’m Daniel, a senior software engineer based in Toronto, with around 7 years of experience building SaaS products and internal platforms. My background started mostly in frontend and product engineering, but over the last couple of years I’ve moved deeper into full-stack development and AI-enabled applications. These days I’m spending most of my time figuring out how to take an AI capability from “interesting prototype” to something customers can actually use every day. My main stack is TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and AWS, with Python coming in whenever the AI/data side needs it. A few things I’ve been working on recently: • Building AI features directly into existing SaaS products rather than treating AI as a separate application • Designing RAG and tool-calling workflows around customer data and internal APIs • Building TypeScript services and React interfaces for AI-assisted workflows • Working with PostgreSQL, Redis, queues, and event-driven architectures for production workloads • Using Docker, AWS, CI/CD, and observability tooling to keep things boring once they reach production One thing I’ve learned recently is that the interesting engineering problem isn’t really “how do we call the model?” It’s everything around it — permissions, state, latency, retries, data quality, UX, and knowing when the system should not use AI. I’m especially interested in connecting with people working on AI-native products, developer tooling, agent workflows, and modern SaaS architecture. Happy to compare notes, collaborate, or help out where I can! 10:44 PM. 3 replies.

Run GPU workloads on preemptible capacity at a fraction of on-demand pricing:
Spot GPU sandboxes are now live for everyone!
spot GPUs don't count against your GPU quota. Available capacity is the only limit.
significantly cheaper than on-demand GPUs, see the pricing page:
H100, H200, RTX Pro 6000, RTX 4090, RTX 5090, with ordered fallback between types.
Getting started: choose a GPU, set resources, and use any Docker image:
sandbox = daytona.create( CreateSandboxFromImageParams( image="nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04", auto_delete_interval=0, spot=True, resources=Resources(gpu=1, gpu_type=GpuType.H100), ) )

Heads up: spot sandboxes are preemptible. They can be reclaimed at any time when on-demand capacity is needed, so design workloads to tolerate interruption. Preempted sandboxes get a spotEvictedAt timestamp and stay retrievable for 24 hours. Try it: https://app.daytona.io/ Docs: https://www.daytona.io/docs/sandboxes#spot-gpu-sandboxes Questions?
